毎.meaning: A <part>mother</part> stands in the pool under a <part>diving board</part>, catching her kids as they jump. One kid, then the next, then the first one again. Nobody gets skipped: she catches <kanji>every</kanji> single one.
毎.on: Then the <sound>mi</sound>ce line up on the diving board too, and she catches every one of them.
毎.kun: Every kid pulls on <sound>go</sound>ggles and climbs back up a <sound>to</sound>tem pole to the board.

十.meaning: Two sticks crossed into a plus sign: one lying flat, one standing up. A teacher taps it on the board: add them up, add again, keep going. The class runs out of fingers right at <kanji>ten</kanji>.
十.on: A thief drops a <sound>jew</sound>el down a drain grate shaped like a plus sign, and ten people dive in after it.
十.kun: Out of fingers, you keep counting down to your last little <sound>toe</sound>.

干.meaning: A <part>one</part>-plank bar is nailed on top of a <part>ten</part> cross, and it becomes a rack in the yard. Wet socks hang from both bars, then a wet cat climbs on too. They all drip in the sun until every one is <kanji>dry</kanji>.
干.on: A pink <sound>car</sound>nation hangs from the rack too, drying for a flower press.
干.kun: Next you hang a wet <sound>ho</sound>tdog on the rack, and a roll of <sound>su</sound>shi beside it.

年.meaning: Under a <part>diving board</part> stands a <part>drying rack</part>. Every summer you hang your towel on it after the first dive, and every summer the towel is a little more faded. Count the faded towels and you know how many have passed, one per <kanji>year</kanji>.
年.on: Once a year the bed li<sound>nen</sound> goes out on the rack too, and comes back smelling of pool.
年.kun: Every year a <sound>to</sound>tem pole carver adds one more <sound>shee</sound>p to the pole.

朝.meaning: On the left, a <part>sun</part> squeezes up between two <part>ten</part> crosses like a head between fence posts. On the right, the <part>moon</part> is still hanging about, yawning. The sun is up and the moon hasn't gone home yet: it's early <kanji>morning</kanji>.
朝.on: Before it leaves, the moon puts on a sparkly <sound>cho</sound>ker so the sun can't outshine it.
朝.kun: The sun yawns '<sound>Ah</sound>…' and opens a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines for breakfast.

外.meaning: One <part>evening</part>, someone leaves the garden <part>faucet</part> running. Nobody indoors notices. By morning the lawn is a pond and ducks have moved in. That's what happens when you forget about things <kanji>outside</kanji>.
外.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog leads you out to the faucet in the dark and turns it off with its nose.
外.kun: Out on the flooded lawn a <sound>so</sound>fa bobs in the water, and a <sound>to</sound>tem pole floats past.

王.meaning: Three planks stacked up like a tall throne, one post nailed straight through the middle of them. Whoever sits on the top plank, feet on the bottom one and elbows on the middle, gives the orders. He's the <kanji>king</kanji>.
王.on: The king's throne is carved from one huge <sound>oa</sound>k, and acorns keep dropping on his crown.

国.meaning: A <part>king</part> stands inside a big <part>cage</part> of walls, a <part>dot</part> of a jewel in his pocket. Everything inside the walls is his: the fields, the towns, the grumpy goats. The walls mark the edge of his <kanji>country</kanji>.
国.on: A <sound>cock</sound>atoo sits on the wall and screams at anyone who tries to cross the border.
国.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo guards the gate in the wall and pecks every visitor on the k<sound>nee</sound>.

金.meaning: A <part>king</part> hides under an <part>umbrella</part>, two little <part>horns</part> of nuggets tucked in beside him. It isn't raining. He just doesn't want anyone to see the shine of his <kanji>gold</kanji>.
金.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher dives down and snatches a nugget from right under the umbrella.
金.kun: The king stuffs his gold into a <sound>ca</sound>r boot and a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t, then goes shopping with it: money.

痛.meaning: In a <part>leaky shed</part>, a <part>pizza wedge</part> balances on top of a wobbly <part>fence</part>. You lean on the fence to reach the pizza, a drip hits your eye, the fence gives way and you land on a nail. Ow: <kanji>pain</kanji>.
痛.on: You hiss through your teeth like a kettle, '<sound>Tsooo</sound>!', and hop around the shed.
痛.kun: You squeal '<sound>Ee</sound>!', kick a <sound>tu</sound>b across the shed and squeal '<sound>Ee</sound>!' again.

品.meaning: Three <part>mouth</part> boxes are stacked in a pyramid on a shop shelf, one on top and two below. Each is wrapped and ready, with a little label that says 'take me home'. A shop full of boxes like that is full of <kanji>goods</kanji>.
品.on: The shop door swings on a squeaky <sound>hin</sound>ge every time someone carries a box out.
品.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p nudges a box of <sound>na</sound>an along the shelf and the whole pyramid of boxes topples.

切.meaning: A <part>spoon</part> tries to slice the birthday cake and just squashes it flat. Then a <part>sword</part> swoops in, one clean swing, and the cake falls into two neat halves. Spoons scoop, swords <kanji>cut</kanji>.
切.on: A red <sound>set</sound>ter dog grabs the bigger half and runs off with it.
切.kun: The sword's next swing cuts a brass <sound>key</sound> in half, and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> catches the pieces.

門.meaning: Two tall doors stand face to face, each with two little windows up top and a long post down to the ground. Fling them both wide and the whole town parade can march through. That's a <kanji>gate</kanji>.
門.on: A <sound>mon</sound>ster guards the gate and only lets in visitors who bring snacks.
門.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>r towing a <sound>do</sound>lphin in a trailer swings past the gate too fast and clips its edge: a corner.

間.meaning: The two <part>gate</part> doors stand slightly apart, and the <part>sun</part> peeks through the crack between them. Shut them and it's dark; open them a little and a strip of light shines in. That narrow strip is the <kanji>interval</kanji>, the space in between.
間.on: Someone slides a single <sound>car</sound>nation into the gap between the doors.
間.kun: You press one <sound>eye</sound> to the gap and see a <sound>du</sound>ck staring back.

開.meaning: Inside a <part>gate</part> stands a soccer <part>goal</part> with a <part>one</part>-plank crossbar on top. A kid kicks the ball, it slams into the gate doors, and they swing wide. Goal! And the gate is <kanji>open</kanji>.
開.on: The ball sails out through the open gate and tangles in a <sound>ki</sound>te string.
開.kun: The fans go wild: a <sound>hee</sound>l kicked high, a '<sound>Rah</sound>!', and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo popping out of the clock.

昼.meaning: A <part>flag</part> flaps on its pole with a <part>dot</part> of a bird on top. Under it the <part>sun</part> blazes over a <part>one</part>-plank bench where the whole office eats lunch, squinting, with no shade anywhere. It's the middle of the <kanji>daytime</kanji>.
昼.on: Everyone on the bench is <sound>chew</sound>ing gum after lunch, blowing bubbles in the sun.
昼.kun: Someone kicks off a high <sound>hee</sound>l to sunbathe, and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> hops off with it.

館.meaning: On the left, a plate of <part>food</part>. On the right, a <part>roof</part> covers two stacked <part>mouth</part> windows joined by a <part>pole</part> of a staircase. Dinner waiting by the door and floor piled on floor: it's a huge <kanji>building</kanji>, a mansion with its own kitchen.
館.on: Every room in the mansion has a single <sound>car</sound>nation in a vase.
館.kun: '<sound>Yah</sound>!' you shout in the hall, and a <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of a marble <sound>tu</sound>b.

夜.meaning: Someone puts a <part>lid</part> on the <part>evening</part> like a pot, and the last light goes out. You hang your coat on the <part>coat hook</part>, and outside the moon is the only lamp left. It's <kanji>night</kanji>.
夜.on: In the dark, the cat finds a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn and unwinds it all over the house.
夜.kun: Half asleep, you eat a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt by moonlight while a kanga<sound>roo</sound> snores under the coat hook.

米.meaning: A cross in the middle, with four little strokes flying off its corners. Someone has dropped a sack, and the grains have bounced out from the center in every direction. Sweep them up and cook them: <kanji>rice</kanji>.
米.on: The sack falls off a boat into the <sound>bay</sound>, and grains float all over the water.
米.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala eats the rice off a <sound>me</sound>tal plate, one grain at a time.

来.meaning: A plank lies on top of a heap of <part>rice</part>, like a sign over a market stall. A single grain falls off, and every pigeon in the city hears it. Wings everywhere: drop rice, and the birds will <kanji>come</kanji>.
来.on: Then a <sound>rhi</sound>no smells the rice and comes too, and the pigeons scatter.
来.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> come running for the rice as well.

茶.meaning: <part>grass</part> sprouts on top of an <part>umbrella</part>, and under the umbrella grows a small <part>tree</part>. You pick its leaves, dry them in the sun and pour hot water over them. The cup turns green: <kanji>tea</kanji>.
茶.on: After two cups of tea, Grandma gets up and dances the <sound>cha</sound>-cha.

面.meaning: A flat bar like a headband, and under it a big box with an eye-shaped box inside. It's a face with no expression at all, painted on wood and tied on with string. Put it on and nobody knows who you are: a <kanji>mask</kanji>.
面.on: At the café, the waiter in the mask hands you a <sound>men</sound>u and won't say a word.
面.kun: You lift the mask. '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a <sound>mo</sound>le, and a <sound>te</sound>nor sings to your bare face.

肉.meaning: Inside a butcher's <part>frame</part> hang two <part>person</part>-shaped hooks, one above the other, each holding a dripping slab. The butcher waves a cleaver at the window. Nothing in this shop is a vegetable: it's all <kanji>meat</kanji>.
肉.on: The butcher drops a slab on his k<sound>nee</sound>, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo bursts out of the clock to laugh.
肉.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p and then another <sound>shee</sound>p peer through the window and quickly walk away.

半.meaning: A goat's two <part>horns</part> poke up behind a <part>two</part>-plank shelf with a cake on it. A <part>pole</part> drops straight down through the middle of it all, splitting goat, shelf and cake into even sides. Everything is cut exactly in <kanji>half</kanji>.
半.on: The goat licks the <sound>hon</sound>ey off its half of the cake.
半.kun: Halfway through, the goat swaps its half for <sound>na</sound>an, a <sound>ca</sound>rp and a <sound>ba</sound>rbecue rib.

体.meaning: A <part>coat hook</part> stands next to a <part>tree</part> with a <part>one</part>-plank bar across its trunk. Hang a jacket on the hook and trousers over the bar, and it looks just like a person standing there. Coat on top, legs below: a whole <kanji>body</kanji>.
体.on: To finish the scarecrow body, you knot a <sound>tie</sound> round the tree trunk.
体.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>r drives by, the driver shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!', and a <sound>du</sound>ck lands on the body's head.

三.meaning: Put a <part>one</part> stroke on top of a <part>two</part>, and you get a stack of planks like a ladder lying down. A cat naps on each plank. Count the cats from top to bottom: one, two, <kanji>three</kanji>.
三.on: Three cats, but you buy just one ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae and three spoons.
三.kun: '<sound>Meet</sound> my cats,' says a meerkat, and all three of them sneeze '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

者.meaning: A <part>stuck javelin</part> stands in the grass above a <part>sun</part>-shaped scoreboard. Who threw it? Nobody saw. There are footprints and a sweaty towel, so it was <kanji>someone</kanji>.
者.on: Someone also left a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock stuck on the javelin's tip.
者.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>le pops out of the grass and shouts '<sound>No</sound>! Not me!'

旅.meaning: A <part>sail</part> on the left, a <part>diving board</part> on the right, and a <part>slash</part> of rope tying them together. You pack a bag, hoist the sail and dive off the board onto the deck. Wave goodbye: you're off on a <kanji>trip</kanji>.
旅.on: You pack one glass of <sound>Rio</sound>ja for the trip and sip it on deck.
旅.kun: On deck you soak in a <sound>tu</sound>b of seawater, with a <sound>bee</sound>tle as your only crew.

券.meaning: Two <part>horns</part> poke over a <part>two</part>-plank barrier where a <part>person</part> sits in a booth, a little <part>sword</part> in hand. You hand over a coin, and the sword slices a paper strip off the roll for you. No strip, no entry: that's your <kanji>ticket</kanji>.
券.on: Your ticket is for the dog show, so you hand it in at the <sound>ken</sound>nel door.

回.meaning: A small <part>mouth</part> is trapped inside a big <part>cage</part>, and it runs laps along the inside walls like a hamster. Round and round it goes, counting as it runs: one, two, five, twenty <kanji>times</kanji>, until it's dizzy.
回.on: A <sound>ki</sound>te string is tied to the mouth, and the kite circles over the cage with it.
回.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>! <sound>Wah</sound>!' cries the dizzy mouth, as a kanga<sound>roo</sound> spins the cage.
